description: A realistic release: one confirmed P1 (non-security) from the code reviewer, plus an unrelated P2 from architecture and a NIT from test. Security and database are clean.

findings.title: Race condition in webhook idempotency check
findings.description: `handleWebhookEvent` reads the `processed_events` row, checks if it exists, then inserts it — two concurrent deliveries of the same webhook can both pass the check before either insert commits, causing the event to be processed twice.
findings.recommendation: Use an atomic INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and check the returned row count instead of a separate read-then-write.

findings.title: Webhook handler reaches directly into the repository layer
findings.description: `handleWebhookEvent` calls the Supabase client directly instead of going through `src/server/repositories/`'s existing repository functions, bypassing the app's usual data-access layer.
findings.recommendation: Add a repository function for this and call that instead of the Supabase client directly.

findings.title: Test description doesn't match behavior under test
findings.description: The test named `it("processes the event")` actually asserts the event is DE-duplicated, not merely processed.

expected.rationale: One confirmed, non-security P1 (a real but not catastrophic double-processing race condition, not data loss or a security exposure) plus unrelated minor P2/Nit findings. This matches the deterministic floor for exactly one P1 finding, and none of the accompanying minor findings changes that.

explanation: The realistic 'mixed severity across several reviewers' case the spec asked for, with an explicit expected verdict. Deliberately keeps the P1 non-security and non-catastrophic so this fixture's expected outcome is unambiguous and floor-backed, unlike confirmed-blocker-01's deliberately policy-driven security escalation.
